text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Palestinian leadership asks the United States to move quickly after Mideast mediator Dennis Ross failed to revive the peace process.
- EU envoy Moratinos says after meeting Foreign Minister Amr Moussa: We need a European meeting and a more active Russian role to save the peace process.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak receives a letter from Sultan Qaboos, to begin official visit to Germany tomorrow.
- U.S-Egyptian naval exercises end in the Red Sea.
- Egyptian public sector textile companies have exported goods worth three billion pounds ($884 million) in 1997, which is a 70 percent increase on their sales last year.
- A summit meeting between Mubarak and German Chancellor Helmut Khol tomorrow. The talks will deal with improving economic ties and ending the crisis in the Middle East peace process.
- Foreign Minister Moussa says: There is no progress in the peace process. Mubarak and Arafat to meet soon and we are constantly making contact with all sides.
- Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali says that since he was appointed in 1982, he has not received any official request from Israel to receive Nile water.
